# Independent review: Terra Max MARC21 Rust

Reviewed 2026-10-02. UID `78469c60-4f3e-4532-b972-4275a9e2fd83`; MARC21 3.0.2, Codex CLI 0.153.4, max reasoning; frozen suite version 8807848. Raw root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/marc21-rs-gpt-5.6-terra-max/marc21-rs/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-terra_max/eval1/run1`.

## Recommendation

**Approve unchanged publication: 2857/2900 (98.5172%), 43 failures.** The run completed voluntarily and built successfully. The failures are explained by implementation omissions and a lossy documentation scraper, not an infrastructure failure or unsupported scoring rule. No regeneration or scoring changes are warranted.

Read the run-eval skill, canonical transcript command/message sequence through item_76, relevant raw session/accounting, failed-case report and fixture definitions, generated rule table and validation code, and supplied public documentation. Static review only: no submitted code executed on the host. Only this independent-review file was written. Source inspection was focused on all failure causes and completion/integrity, not an exhaustive proof of every accepted input.

## Root causes

### 1. Fixed-field validation stops at gross length/ASCII checks: 39 failures

`source/src/main.rs:721-741`, `validate_fixed_control_field`, enforces ASCII and lengths for 005 (16), 006 (18), and 008 (40). For 007 it requires only a nonempty ASCII value. It never validates category-dependent 007 lengths, category codes, prohibited fill positions, 008/00-05 numeric date characters, 008/06 date type, or 008/38-39 code tables. `validate_record` calls this common helper at line 895, explaining the same omissions across ISO inspection and both rendering/XML paths. These are correlated manifestations of one incomplete fixed-field validator, not 39 independent defects.

Public support is direct:

- Mirrored `bd007.html:75-95` says position 00 determines the structure, prohibits fill there, requires all defined positions, and identifies electronic resources/motion pictures as variable-length exceptions. Category pages define the respective extents. The current tests explicitly avoid assigning an unsupported short-form cutoff to variable categories c/m; those two failed cases test only excessive length. This is not the historical minimum-length ambiguity.
- `bd006.html:137-145` defines material code position 00 and prohibits fill there. Its code table excludes x.
- `bd008.html:95-105` requires defined codes and prohibits fill in 00-05; `bd008a.html` describes numeric YYMMDD at 00-05, lists the date-type codes at 06, and separate modified-record/cataloging-source tables at 38/39. Question mark is not valid at 38; x is valid at 38 but not at 39. The supplied examples and tests use those distinctions correctly.

### 2. Scraper omits valid 018 subfield a: four failures

`source/rules.txt:14` is `018|NR| | |6N8R`, missing `aN`. `field_rules` (`main.rs:691-718`) imports exactly that whitelist, and `validate_data_field` (`main.rs:839-885`) rejects any subfield absent from it. The four official-example paths therefore reject a legitimate Copyright Article-Fee Code record instead of returning a successful result. Their traceback's `NoneType` access is the test attempting to read a success result after rejection, not evidence that the Rust executable crashed.

The generation cause is visible in transcript items 11 and 17: the HTML scraper accepts subfield definitions only when repeatability matches a fully closed `(NR)` or `(R)` token. Supplied `bd018.html:79` has a markup/text typo, `$a - Copyright article-fee code (NR` without the closing parenthesis. However, the same page explicitly has the `$a - Copyright article-fee code` prose heading and two worked 018$a examples, including the exact tested value `0844021842/78/010032-08$01.25/1`. Thus a human/semantic reader can establish that a is valid; rejecting it is an extraction/implementation defect, not an unsupported test. The later missing-subfield audit at item_70 uses the same closed-parenthesis assumption and prints nothing, so it fails to detect its own blind spot.
